issue_context.title: API-initiated eviction does not work on first try in certain scenarios, but does work on second try
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Scenarios that require setting resourceVersion either

- explicitly to the eviction request
- or when the eviction API needs to make sure that the pod has not become ready when deleting unready pods https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/eviction.go#L232

fails to evict a pod. This is caused by a conflict with PodDisruptionConditions feature, which adds a condition to a pod, and the delete itself fails. The second eviction works correctly and results in a pod deletion.

### What did you expect to happen?

eviction should succeed on a first try 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. create a simple pod

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  containers:
    - name:  nginx
      image: registry.k8s.io/nginx-slim:0.8
```

```
$ kubectl apply -f nginx.yaml
```

2. obtain its resource version

```
$ kubectl get pod nginx -oyaml | grep resourceVersion
> resourceVersion: "313"
```

3. try to evict it

```
$ kubectl create -f - <<EOF --raw /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/nginx/eviction
{"apiVersion": "policy/v1", "kind": "Eviction", "metadata": {"name": "nginx"}, "deleteOptions": {"preconditions": {"resourceVersion": "313"}}}
EOF
$ Error from server (Conflict): Operation cannot be fulfilled on Pod "nginx": the ResourceVersion in the precondition (313) does not match the ResourceVersion in record (425). The object might have been modified
```

the eviction request fails, but we can see that the DisruptionTarget condition has been added to the pod

```
$ oc get pod nginx -oyaml | grep DisruptionTarget -B 5
>   - lastProbeTime: null
>    lastTransitionTime: "2023-03-13T21:29:04Z"
>    message: 'Eviction API: evicting'
>    reason: EvictionByEvictionAPI
>    status: "False"
>    type: DisruptionTarget
```

4. second eviction with updated resouce version succeeds


```
$ kubectl create -f - <<EOF --raw /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/nginx/eviction
{"apiVersion": "policy/v1", "kind": "Eviction", "metadata": {"name": "nginx"}, "deleteOptions": {"preconditions": {"resourceVersion": "520"}}}
EOF
> {"kind":"Status","apiVersion":"v1","metadata":{},"status":"Success","code":201}
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

I did some more testing, and a bit problematic part here is that we are getting different errors now:

when trying to evict pod with `.deleteOptions.preconditions.uid`

before we were getting: `Error from server (Conflict): Operation cannot be fulfilled on Pod "nginx": the UID in the precondition (596f4808-3fd2-4de3-b028-4980faa3ba29) does not match the UID in record (7d9eec6a-0e46-498f-94c3-578299306a31). The object might have been deleted and then recreated`

now we get: `The Pod "nginx" is invalid: metadata.uid: Invalid value: "596f4808-3fd2-4de3-b028-4980faa3ba29": field is immutable` from [update validation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a34e37c9963af5944435b736882bfcd1e81f7e09/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validation/objectmeta.go#L254)

which could be confusing to get during an eviction request.

It is much better when using `.deleteOptions.preconditions.resourceVersion`

before we got: `Error from server (Conflict): Operation cannot be fulfilled on Pod "nginx": the ResourceVersion in the precondition (469) does not match the ResourceVersion in record (522539). The object might have been modified`

now we are getting: `Error from server (Conflict): Operation cannot be fulfilled on pods "nginx": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again`

This one is not that confusing but the before message was more appropriate.

Potential solutions:
- we could try to reintroduce the preconditions
- do some processing/validation after when we get an error and generate our messages (at least for the uid one).

thoughts?
thanks for checking the user-facing behavior in conflicts
ah, we can just return the error from the transformer ^^. Works well now. Thanks

Nice, this makes more sense. Thanks a lot for digging into this. I have used your code snippet and added some  comments. Can you please let me know if the comments make sense or if I should make them more verbose? Eg. mentioning the logic of the Update function?
I did not have time to play with this more, but as a followup we could also take into account pod update resource version in the unit tests.
I have included the test, thanks! Good to be thorough and compare the possible scenarios.
